ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible transaction semantics for workflow/tool orchestration under H1-H8 is: (i) for all effects on media the system controls — strict-serializable, single-commit-point atomicity: a multi-object transition (the six-item set of STORAGE-API.sexp) becomes visible through exactly one atomic switch, with durability exactly at the platform's fsync barrier and read-back-verified persistence, such that after a crash at ANY instant the recovered state is exactly sigma_pre or exactly sigma_post — never a hybrid; (ii) for effects on media the system does NOT control (network calls to external tools/publishers) — exactly-once is unattainable; the ceiling is journaled intent/outcome with idempotency keys and compensations, with the irrevocable external act structurally excluded from the atomic section. No feasible system exceeds (i) or circumvents (ii).
derivation: (i) is a storage-physics and protocol-theory bound. Stable storage exposes only bounded atomic units (a sector / an atomic rename of a directory entry) and reorders un-fenced writes; therefore any multi-object atomicity must be MANUFACTURED by funneling all objects' validity through one atomic commit record reached after fsync barriers — write-ahead logging and shadow-paging are the only two families, and both bottom out in a single atomic pointer/record switch. You cannot be 'more atomic' than one atomic switch, and you cannot be durable earlier than the fsync that puts the commit record on stable media: before that instant the information physically is not on the medium, so no protocol can promise it survives power loss. Read-back verification is the ceiling of durability EVIDENCE (H8: never trust a declared write). (ii) is the atomic-commitment impossibility: committing atomically across parties with independent failure modes requires a coordinator round (2PC), which blocks on coordinator failure and in the two-generals limit cannot be made both non-blocking and safe; since external publishers/tools grant the system no transactional interface at all, the honest ceiling is intent-journal before the call, outcome-journal after, idempotency keys for at-least-once retry, and compensation — with H3 demanding that an unknowable external outcome parks the workflow in a typed UNKNOWN state (H2) rather than guessing. H6 then fixes the composition: a workflow of many tool steps is accountable only if every trusted-state mutation routes through the single atomic commit of (i), making 'partial workflow effects in the canonical store' structurally impossible rather than guarded — exactly the error-class-elimination the supreme law demands.
attainment_mechanism: Implement commit-accepted-transition! of authority-v2/store/STORAGE-API.sexp as a shadow-commit protocol in SBCL with sb-posix (all available today): (1) write the six items (accepted-transition CBOR, state-sequence, release-reference, C2SP log entry, signed checkpoint, latest pointer target) to temp files inside the store filesystem; fsync each fd; (2) write a commit record naming the six items with their SHA-256 (seat: source/hash-authority.lisp) and the new sequence; fsync it; fsync the directory; (3) atomically rename the commit record to its final name — this rename IS the single commit point; fsync the directory; (4) recovery scans for the commit record, recomputes all six hashes (recompute-and-compare, same discipline as source/authority-evidence-replay.lisp), rolls forward a complete commit or removes orphan temps — provably sigma_pre or sigma_post; (5) read-back verification after commit as already practiced by orchestrator.journal:require-durable! (used at source/adoption-decision.lisp:99); (6) the single-writer premise of the protocol is the already-proven OS-DAC closure (authority-v2/proofs/verify-capability-closure.sh); (7) external tool calls (e.g. source/government-source.lisp fetches) move to an intent/outcome journal with idempotency keys OUTSIDE the atomic section, their products entering the store only as candidates through the commit. The creator's STORAGE-API prohibition targets crash-TESTS as the assurance substrate; the ceiling mechanism satisfies its intent by discharging the atomicity/recovery obligations as a machine-checked Lean 4 crash-refinement proof (the obligation below) in place of the externally-blocked Perennial/GoTxn route — proof, not tests, remains the substrate.
b0_gap: B0's sharpest hole (B0 map AX-15/AX-11 rows): the six-item transaction is specification-only — authority-v2/store/STORAGE-API.sexp declares :implementation-status :absent-by-design, :production-writer :disabled, with atomicity/recovery obligations :blocked-toolchain; meanwhile the actual canonical artifact writer emit-graph (source/write-authority.lisp:47) opens with :if-exists :supersede and no fsync or temp-rename, so a crash mid-write leaves a truncated canonical .ttl — the exact hybrid state the ceiling forbids. Durability discipline (require-durable!) exists only for governance ledgers (source/adoption-decision.lisp, source/memory.lisp), not the artifact path. External tool calls have no intent/outcome journal. The gap is therefore the entire clause (i) implementation plus the Lean proof standing in for the blocked Perennial obligation, and clause (ii)'s journal.
lean_obligation: Model a POSIX-like disk as a labeled transition system D with operations write(addr,bytes), fsync(fd), fsyncdir, rename(a,b) where rename of a directory entry is atomic, un-fsynced writes may be arbitrarily reordered/dropped at a crash, and crash is enabled at every step. Let P be the commit protocol program and R the recovery function. Prove crash refinement of the atomic specification: forall disk behaviors b of (P;crash*;R), the recovered abstract state alpha(R(b)) = sigma_pre OR alpha(R(b)) = sigma_post, and alpha(R(b)) = sigma_post iff the commit-record rename was durably applied; plus recovery idempotence: R(R(b)) = R(b); plus durability soundness: if P returns success then every subsequent crash recovers sigma_post.
